snapshot.stmt: Can the handle \(\mathsf{SAR}_{x,y,n}\) be completed into a computable confidence set \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{SAR}}_{x,y,n,1-\alpha}\) such that, for deterministic \(n_s(n)+n_t(n)=n\) with \(n\to\infty\) and \(n_s(n)/n\to p\in(0,1)\), \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb M\in\mathcal A_p}\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}\{\theta_{x,y,n}\in\widehat C^{\mathrm{SAR}}_{x,y,n,1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\]? Here \(\mathcal A_p\) retains exactly the target-span restriction while permitting changing rank of \(B_{x,n}\), singular joint multinomial covariance, and diverging minimum-norm balancing weights. For every \(1\le r_0\le\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\), fixed \(c,\eta>0\), and fixed \(\mathcal M\in\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}\), with the associated constant array \(\mathcal M_n=\mathcal M\), can the same set also satisfy the determinate regular-branch requirements \(\operatorname{diam}_2(\widehat C^{\mathrm{SAR}}_{x,y,n,1-\alpha})=O_P(n^{-1/2})\) and \(\sqrt n\,d_H(\widehat C^{\mathrm{SAR}}_{x,y,n,1-\alpha},I^W_{n,1-\alpha})\to_P0\) under the stated allocation regime?

defs.def:euclidean-hausdorff-distance: For nonempty \(C,D\subseteq[0,1]\), \(d_H(C,D)=\max\{\sup_{\xi\in C}\inf_{\zeta\in D}|\xi-\zeta|,\sup_{\zeta\in D}\inf_{\xi\in C}|\xi-\zeta|\}\), the Euclidean Hausdorff distance.
defs.def:regular-wald-functional: For \(H\in\mathbb R^{m\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), \(z\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), define \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)=z^{\top}H_{r_0}^{\dagger}b\), where \(H_{r_0}\) is the rank-\(r_0\) truncated-SVD matrix.
defs.def:regular-wald-variance: \(\widehat V_n\) is the plug-in delta-method variance for \(\phi_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n)\), using the joint source multinomial covariance and target multinomial covariance with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\).
defs.def:strongly-identified-submodel: For \(1\le r_0\le\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\) and fixed \(c,\eta>0\), \(\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}:\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0,\ \sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c,\ b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x),\ z_{x,y}\in\operatorname{row}(H_x),\text{ every source and target cell is at least }\eta,\text{ and }V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta\}\).
defs.def:studentized-array-class: \(\mathcal A_p=\{\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}:\mathbb M\text{ obeys the fixed-proportion allocation and row-wise independent two-sample conditions, and }b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})\text{ for every }n\ge2\}\). No restriction is imposed on changes in \(\operatorname{rank}(B_{x,n})\), singularity of the joint multinomial covariance, or divergence of \(d_{x,n}\).
defs.def:studentized-projection-handle: At row \(n\), begin from the joint restrictions \(H_{x,n}\kappa=b_n\) and \(z_{x,y,n}^{\top}\kappa=\theta_{x,y,n}\), estimated by \(\widehat H_{x,n}\), \(\widehat z_{x,y,n}\), and \(\widehat b_n\). Retain stochastic covariance directions and impose exact simplex directions separately using singularity-robust standardization, invert the full \((\theta_{x,y,n},\kappa)\) test, and project over unrestricted \(\kappa\) to construct \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{SAR}}_{x,y,n,1-\alpha}\) along arrays in \(\mathcal A_p\).

assumptions.ass:array-target-span: For every \(n\), the row-\(n\) target proxy law satisfies \(b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})\).
assumptions.ass:triangular-allocation: The sequences \(n_s(n)\) and \(n_t(n)\) are deterministic, \(n_s(n)+n_t(n)=n\) for every \(n\), \(n\to\infty\), and \(n_s(n)/n\to p\in(0,1)\).
assumptions.ass:triangular-sample-independence: For every \(n\), the row-\(n\) source sample is independent of the row-\(n\) target sample.
assumptions.ass:triangular-source-iid-sampling: For every \(n\), the observations \(O^s_{1,n},\ldots,O^s_{n_s(n),n}\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_{O,n}\).
assumptions.ass:triangular-target-iid-sampling: For every \(n\), the observations \(W^t_{1,n},\ldots,W^t_{n_t(n),n}\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(b_n\).
assumptions.ass:regular-fixed-rank: The fixed source moment matrix satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0\).
assumptions.ass:regular-singular-gap: The smallest retained singular value satisfies \(\sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c\).
assumptions.ass:regular-target-span: The fixed target proxy vector satisfies \(b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x)\).
assumptions.ass:regular-outcome-row: The fixed outcome moment vector satisfies \(z_{x,y}\in\operatorname{row}(H_x)\).
assumptions.ass:regular-cell-floor: The minimum over all source observed cells and target proxy cells satisfies \(\min\bigl(\{P_O(e,w,x,y):e\in\mathcal E,w\in\mathcal W,x\in\mathcal X,y\in\mathcal Y\}\cup\{b_w:w\in\mathcal W\}\bigr)\ge\eta\).
assumptions.ass:regular-positive-variance: The population delta-method variance satisfies \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta\).

snapshot.stmt: For every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\), \(B_x=MR_x\), \(b=Mq\), \(c_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}R_x\), and \(\theta_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}q\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\). Moreover, every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) and its unconditional weight map \(\kappa\) satisfy \(H_x\kappa=b\) and \(z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa=\theta_{x,y}\).

assumptions.ass:strict-primitive-positivity: Every entry of \(\pi\), \(S\), \(M\), \(a\), \(f\), and \(q\) is strictly positive.

snapshot.stmt: If \(b\in\operatorname{col}(B_x)\), then for every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\), every sample size pair \((n_s,n_t)\), and every \(0<\alpha<1\), \(\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}\{\theta_{x,y}\in\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\). defs.def:concentration-projection-set: Let \(L=m\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+m\), \(r_s=\sqrt{\log(2L/\alpha)/(2n_s)}\), and \(r_t=\sqrt{\log(2L/\alpha)/(2n_t)}\). Define \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}=\{\vartheta\in[0,1]:\exists\kappa\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert},\ \lVert\widehat H_x\kappa-\widehat b\rVert_{\infty}\le r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1+r_t,\ |\widehat z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa-\vartheta|\le r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1\}\).

assumptions.ass:sample-source-independence: The source sample is independent of the target sample.
assumptions.ass:source-iid-sampling: The observations \(O_1^s,\ldots,O_{n_s}^s\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_O\).
assumptions.ass:target-iid-sampling: The observations \(W_1^t,\ldots,W_{n_t}^t\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(b\).

snapshot.stmt:
The requested simultaneous conclusion is false on the stated unrestricted array class.  More precisely, fix \(p\in(0,1)\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  There is an admissible instance with binary \(E,U,W,Y\), singleton \(\mathcal X=\{x\}\), a fixed model in \(\mathcal R_{1,1/4,1/16}\), and an array \(\mathbb M\in\mathcal A_p\) such that the fixed model has \(\theta_{x,1}=1/2\), every row of the array has \(\theta_{x,1,n}=5/8\), and the two induced two-sample laws become arbitrarily close in total variation.  Consequently, no sequence of measurable data-dependent nonempty sets \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{SAR}}_{x,1,n,1-\alpha}\) can satisfy both
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb M\in\mathcal A_p}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\{\theta_{x,1,n}\in\widehat C^{\mathrm{SAR}}_{x,1,n,1-\alpha}\}
\ge 1-\alpha
\]
and the asserted fixed-regular requirement
\[
\sqrt n\,d_H\!\left(\widehat C^{\mathrm{SAR}}_{x,1,n,1-\alpha},
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\right)\longrightarrow_P0
\]
for every fixed model in every \(\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}\).  Hence no completion of \(\mathsf{SAR}_{x,y,n}\) can have all the properties in the question without restricting \(\mathcal A_p\).  The uniform-coverage half alone remains attainable: the row-indexed version of \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\) from the concentration projection theorem has the displayed uniform coverage, including along changing-rank arrays, but the impossibility result shows that it cannot also have the demanded Wald equivalence throughout the present class.

defs.def:concentration-projection-set: Let \(L=m\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+m\), \(r_s=\sqrt{\log(2L/\alpha)/(2n_s)}\), and \(r_t=\sqrt{\log(2L/\alpha)/(2n_t)}\). Define \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}=\{\vartheta\in[0,1]:\exists\kappa\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert},\ \lVert\widehat H_x\kappa-\widehat b\rVert_{\infty}\le r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1+r_t,\ |\widehat z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa-\vartheta|\le r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1\}\).
defs.def:euclidean-hausdorff-distance: For nonempty \(C,D\subseteq[0,1]\), \(d_H(C,D)=\max\{\sup_{\xi\in C}\inf_{\zeta\in D}|\xi-\zeta|,\sup_{\zeta\in D}\inf_{\xi\in C}|\xi-\zeta|\}\), the Euclidean Hausdorff distance.
defs.def:positive-latent-shift-class: \(\mathfrak M_{+}=\{\mathcal M=(\pi,S,M,a,f,q):\mathcal M\text{ satisfies the latent-shift factorization, strict primitive positivity, and }\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\}\).
defs.def:regular-wald-functional: For \(H\in\mathbb R^{m\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), \(z\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), define the scalar function \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)=z^{\top}H_{r_0}^{\dagger}b\), where \(H_{r_0}=H^{\star}_{r_0}\) is the selector-based Gram-spectral truncation fixed in the definition of \(H_{r_0}\). Thus \(\phi_{r_0}\) is single valued at tied cutoffs. If \(\sigma_{r_0}(H)>\sigma_{r_0+1}(H)\), the retained subspace is unique, so both \(H_{r_0}\) and \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)\) are independent of the fixed within-tie selector.
defs.def:regular-wald-variance:
Put \(\widehat T_n=(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n)\), and let \(\widehat\Gamma_n\) be the plug-in covariance matrix of \(\sqrt n\,\widehat T_n\), formed from the joint source multinomial covariance and the target multinomial covariance with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\). The totalized plug-in variance is
\[
\widehat V_n=
\begin{cases}
D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)\,\widehat\Gamma_n\,D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)^{\top},
&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})>\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),\\
0,&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})\le\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),
\end{cases}
\]
where \(D\phi_{r_0}\) is the ordinary derivative of the selector-independent functional on the strict-cutoff-gap region and \(\sigma_{\bar q+1}=0\) for \(\bar q=\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\). The second line is the fixed nonnegative fallback.
defs.def:strongly-identified-submodel: For \(1\le r_0\le\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\) and fixed \(c,\eta>0\), \(\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}:\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0,\ \sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c,\ b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x),\text{ every source and target cell is at least }\eta,\text{ and }V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta\}\).

No restriction is imposed on changes in \(\operatorname{rank}(B_{x,n})\), singularity of the joint multinomial covariance, or divergence of \(d_{x,n}\).

Retain stochastic covariance directions and impose exact simplex directions separately using singularity-robust standardization, invert the full \((\theta_{x,y,n},\kappa)\) test, and project over unrestricted \(\kappa\) to construct \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{SAR}}_{x,y,n,1-\alpha}\) along arrays in \(\mathcal A_p\).

snapshot.stmt: Suppose \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(b\notin\operatorname{col}(B_x)\). For every baseline \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\), every \(y\in\mathcal Y\), and every \(h\in\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)\), there is \(\varepsilon>0\) such that replacing \(f\) by \(f^{(t)}\) yields \(\mathcal M_t\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\) for all \(|t|<\varepsilon\), while \(\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M_t)-\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)=t h^{\top}b\). Hence the compatible values of \(\theta_{x,y}\) contain a nondegenerate open interval around the baseline value.

defs.def:compatible-fiber: \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}:\mathcal M\text{ induces exactly the supplied }P_O\text{ and }b\}\).
defs.def:outcome-null-perturbation: Fix \(h\in\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)\), put \(v=M^{\top}h\), choose \(w_{\star}\in\mathcal W\) and \(y^{\circ}\ne y\), and set \(f^{(t)}_{x,y}(u,w_{\star})=f_{x,y}(u,w_{\star})+t v_u/M_{w_{\star}u}\), \(f^{(t)}_{x,y^{\circ}}(u,w_{\star})=f_{x,y^{\circ}}(u,w_{\star})-t v_u/M_{w_{\star}u}\); every other cell equals \(f\).

defs.def:regular-wald-functional: For \(H\in\mathbb R^{m\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), \(z\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), define the scalar function \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)=z^{\top}H_{r_0}^{\dagger}b\), where \(H_{r_0}=H^{\star}_{r_0}\) is the selector-based Gram-spectral truncation fixed in the definition of \(H_{r_0}\). Thus \(\phi_{r_0}\) is single valued at tied cutoffs. If \(\sigma_{r_0}(H)>\sigma_{r_0+1}(H)\), the retained subspace is unique, so both \(H_{r_0}\) and \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)\) are independent of the fixed within-tie selector.
defs.def:regular-wald-variance:
Put \(\widehat T_n=(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n)\), and let \(\widehat\Gamma_n\) be the plug-in covariance matrix of \(\sqrt n\,\widehat T_n\), formed from the joint source multinomial covariance and the target multinomial covariance with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\). The totalized plug-in variance is
\[
\widehat V_n=
\begin{cases}
D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)\,\widehat\Gamma_n\,D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)^{\top},
&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})>\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),\\
0,&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})\le\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),
\end{cases}
\]
where \(D\phi_{r_0}\) is the ordinary derivative of the selector-independent functional on the strict-cutoff-gap region and \(\sigma_{\bar q+1}=0\) for \(\bar q=\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\). The second line is the fixed nonnegative fallback.
defs.def:strongly-identified-submodel: For \(1\le r_0\le\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\) and fixed \(c,\eta>0\), \(\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}:\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0,\ \sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c,\ b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x),\text{ every source and target cell is at least }\eta,\text{ and }V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta\}\).
defs.def:studentized-array-class: \(\mathcal A_p=\{\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}:\mathbb M\text{ obeys the fixed-proportion allocation and row-wise source and target i.i.d. sampling conditions, and }b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})\text{ for every }n\ge2\}\). No restriction is imposed on changes in \(\operatorname{rank}(B_{x,n})\), singularity of the joint multinomial covariance, or divergence of \(d_{x,n}\).
defs.def:studentized-projection-handle: At row \(n\), begin from the joint restrictions \(H_{x,n}\kappa=b_n\) and \(z_{x,y,n}^{\top}\kappa=\theta_{x,y,n}\), estimated by \(\widehat H_{x,n}\), \(\widehat z_{x,y,n}\), and \(\widehat b_n\). Retain stochastic covariance directions and impose exact simplex directions separately using singularity-robust standardization, invert the full \((\theta_{x,y,n},\kappa)\) test, and project over unrestricted \(\kappa\) to construct \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{SAR}}_{x,y,n,1-\alpha}\) along arrays in \(\mathcal A_p\).

assumptions.ass:array-target-span: For every \(n\), the row-\(n\) target proxy law satisfies \(b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})\).
assumptions.ass:strict-primitive-positivity: Every entry of \(\pi\), \(S\), \(M\), \(a\), \(f\), and \(q\) is strictly positive.
assumptions.ass:triangular-allocation: The sequences \(n_s(n)\) and \(n_t(n)\) are deterministic, \(n_s(n)+n_t(n)=n\) for every \(n\), \(n\to\infty\), and \(n_s(n)/n\to p\in(0,1)\).
assumptions.ass:triangular-source-iid-sampling: For every \(n\), the observations \(O^s_{1,n},\ldots,O^s_{n_s(n),n}\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_{O,n}\).
assumptions.ass:triangular-target-iid-sampling: For every \(n\), the observations \(W^t_{1,n},\ldots,W^t_{n_t(n),n}\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(b_n\).
assumptions.ass:regular-fixed-rank: The fixed source moment matrix satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0\).
assumptions.ass:regular-singular-gap: The smallest retained singular value satisfies \(\sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c\).
assumptions.ass:regular-target-span: The fixed target proxy vector satisfies \(b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x)\).
assumptions.ass:regular-cell-floor: The minimum over all source observed cells and target proxy cells satisfies \(\min\bigl(\{P_O(e,w,x,y):e\in\mathcal E,w\in\mathcal W,x\in\mathcal X,y\in\mathcal Y\}\cup\{b_w:w\in\mathcal W\}\bigr)\ge\eta\).
assumptions.ass:regular-positive-variance: The population delta-method variance satisfies \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta\).

defs.def:concentration-projection-set: Let \(L=m\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+m\), \(r_s=\sqrt{\log(2L/\alpha)/(2n_s)}\), and \(r_t=\sqrt{\log(2L/\alpha)/(2n_t)}\). Define \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}=\{\vartheta\in[0,1]:\exists\kappa\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert},\ \lVert\widehat H_x\kappa-\widehat b\rVert_{\infty}\le r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1+r_t,\ |\widehat z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa-\vartheta|\le r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1\}\).
